sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Tab bar and panel wrappers
sections.what: Builds the four pieces of a tab bar: the container, the row of buttons, each button and each panel. Each has a default look that callers can extend.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the app's tab look in one place. Otherwise reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Each trigger and its content must use the same value, or the panel never appears.

summary: Provides the tab building blocks (tab container, tab buttons and tab panels) styled to match the app.
purpose: Lets a screen show several panels where the user switches between them using tab buttons.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The structure suggests a styled wrapper around a shared accessible tabs library, Radix.
how: Tabs is the container from the Radix library. TabsList is the row of tab buttons. TabsTrigger is one button. TabsContent is the panel shown when its tab is selected. Each wrapper adds default styling and merges in any extra styling the caller passes.
inputs: Props from the Radix library, an optional className for extra styling, and a ref.
outputs: React components that draw the tab markup on screen.
risks: Low. The only logic is styling. Bad class names change looks, not data.
debug: If tabs do not switch, check that each TabsTrigger value matches a TabsContent value in the calling screen. If styling is wrong, check the className the caller passes and the cn helper in lib/utils.
